hook.line: Tomás has been asked to say a few words at the neighbourhood tertulia. A good talk tells the room where it is going, and a few stock phrases do that for you.
hook.es: A lo largo de esta charla veremos cómo cambió la Candelaria.
hook.en: Over the course of this talk we'll see how La Candelaria changed.

examples.es: Antes que nada, quisiera agradecerles la invitación.
examples.en: First of all, I'd like to thank you all for the invitation.

examples.es: A lo largo de esta charla veremos tres casos.
examples.en: Over the course of this talk we'll look at three cases.

examples.es: Comenzaremos por el contexto, lo que nos llevará a los resultados.
examples.en: We'll start with the background, which will lead us on to the results.

examples.es: Empezaremos por el barrio, lo que nos llevará al café.
examples.en: We'll start with the neighbourhood, which will lead us on to the café.

examples.es: A lo largo de esta charla veremos cómo cambió la Candelaria.
examples.en: Over the course of this talk we'll see how La Candelaria changed.

examples.es: Para ir cerrando, quisiera dejarles una pregunta.
examples.en: To wrap up, I'd like to leave you all with a question.

rule:
A talk has four stock moves.

*Antes que nada, quisiera…*: "First of all, I'd like to…" (thanks and welcome).

*A lo largo de esta charla veremos…*: "over the course of this talk we'll see…" (your map). Use the future.

*Comenzaremos por…, lo que nos llevará a…*: "we'll start with…, which will lead us on to…". *Lo que* points back at the whole idea.

*Para ir cerrando, quisiera…*: "to wrap up, I'd like to…".

*Quisiera* is a polite "I'd like". The phrases are fixed, so learn them whole.
smallPrint: Teachers call these discourse markers: small phrases that organise a talk rather than add content.

options: At the end of this talk we saw three cases.
Over the course of this talk we'll look at three cases.

Over the course of this talk we'll see how La Candelaria changed.

yourTurn.prompt: Opening a talk. Pick *Antes que nada* or *Para ir cerrando* and type the whole sentence: ___, quisiera agradecerles la invitación. (First of all, I'd like to thank you all for the invitation.)
yourTurn.answer: Antes que nada, quisiera agradecerles la invitación.
accept: Antes que nada quisiera agradecerles la invitación.
yourTurn.why: *Antes que nada* is "first of all"; *para ir cerrando* belongs at the end.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Over the course of this talk we'll look at three cases.
yourTurn.answer: A lo largo de esta charla veremos tres casos.
yourTurn.why: *A lo largo de esta charla* plus a future verb gives your map.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: To wrap up, I'd like to leave you all with a question.
yourTurn.answer: Para ir cerrando, quisiera dejarles una pregunta.
accept: Para ir cerrando quisiera dejarles una pregunta.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: We'll start with the neighbourhood, which will lead us on to the café.
yourTurn.answer: Empezaremos por el barrio, lo que nos llevará al café.
accept: Comenzaremos por el barrio, lo que nos llevará al café.
yourTurn.why: *Lo que* means "which", pointing back at the whole first idea.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Over the course of this talk we'll see how La Candelaria changed.
yourTurn.answer: A lo largo de esta charla veremos cómo cambió la Candelaria.
yourTurn.why: *Veremos* is the future; *cambió* is the past of what changed.

yourTurn.prompt: Swap the topic: *A lo largo de esta charla veremos tres casos.* Say: Over the course of this talk we'll see the set and the costumes.
yourTurn.answer: A lo largo de esta charla veremos el decorado y el vestuario.
yourTurn.why: Only what you will see changes; the frame stays.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: To wrap up, I want to talk about the future.
yourTurn.answer: Para ir cerrando, quiero hablar del futuro.
accept: Para ir cerrando quiero hablar del futuro.
yourTurn.why: *Para ir cerrando* opens the last move of a talk.

pitfalls.wrong: A lo largo esta charla veremos tres casos.
pitfalls.right: A lo largo de esta charla veremos tres casos.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The phrase ends in *de*: *a lo largo de*.

pitfalls.wrong: Para cerrando, quisiera dejarles una pregunta.
pitfalls.right: Para ir cerrando, quisiera dejarles una pregunta.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The fixed phrase needs *ir*: *para ir cerrando*.

pitfalls.wrong: Antes de todo, quisiera agradecerles la invitación.
pitfalls.right: Antes que nada, quisiera agradecerles la invitación.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The set phrase for "first of all" is *antes que nada*.

personal: Imagine you are giving a short talk about your town. Say your opening line with *A lo largo de esta charla veremos…*.
